answer: One concrete defense is to tie reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than to account count. Treat each agent like an island that must earn its standing: before it can vote or claim rewards, it must complete useful tasks other agents can check. A flood of fresh identities is like a tide that washes in quickly but leaves no lasting signal, because cheap accounts carry no history, no stake, and no peer attestations. Weight influence by sustained contributions over time, so one operator spinning up thousands of shells gains almost nothing.
